header.name: Dabur India Ltd
header.source: NSE closing price (end of day, not live); 52-week range computed from daily highs and lows (NSE bhavcopy)

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Dabur India (NSE: DABUR) sells consumer care products (hair, oral, health and home care) and foods and beverages, and runs a retail business; its consolidated revenue in FY26 was ₹13,193 crore.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: In the quarter to 30 Sep 2026, revenue was ₹3,563 crore, 11.6% more than a year earlier; the operating margin was 14.4% against 14.8%, and profit attributable to shareholders was ₹506 crore, 11.7% higher.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: On 5 Nov 2026, the first session after the result, DABUR shares fell 2.53% while the NIFTY 50 rose 2.40% and the NIFTY FMCG index rose 0.45%; allowing for the market's move, DABUR's own move was -4.63%, about 3.69 times its usual daily variation.

claims.label: UNCERTAIN
claims.text: These numbers measure the move, not its cause: the result, the FMCG sector's rise and any other news that day overlap, and nothing here separates them.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: At ₹382 (NSE close, 16 Nov 2026), a discounted cash flow model with a 10.11% cost of capital matches the price if revenue grows about 19.9% a year for five years at the FY26 operating margin of 15.0%; DABUR's revenue grew 4.9% a year over FY22–FY26.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: With the other assumptions at base, the valuation is most sensitive to the cost of capital (one percentage point either way: a model value of ₹174 to ₹238 a share) and to how long DABUR keeps earning high returns on new investment (anywhere from returns equal to its cost of capital to a quarter above its past level: a model value of ₹158 to ₹203 a share); the Q3 FY27 result will be the next reported quarter.

prices.note: Each series is rebased to 100 on the first common session. Raw exchange prices are not published here (NSE terms).

metrics.label: Market cap
metrics.definition: Price × shares outstanding (share capital ÷ ₹1 face value at 2026-09-30).

metrics.label: P/E (TTM)
metrics.definition: Price ÷ earnings per share over the last four reported quarters (Q3 FY26 – Q2 FY27).

metrics.label: EV / EBIT (TTM)
metrics.definition: Enterprise value (market cap − the net cash and treasury figure below) ÷ operating profit over the last four quarters.

metrics.label: Net cash and treasury
metrics.definition: Cash, bank balances and treasury investments, plus investments in joint ventures and associates, less lease liabilities, borrowings, preference shares and minority interests, at 30 Sep 2026.

metrics.label: Operating margin (FY26)
metrics.definition: EBIT ÷ revenue, after depreciation, excluding other income. Sites that quote an EBITDA-based margin show a higher figure.

metrics.label: ROE (FY26)
metrics.definition: Profit for the year ÷ total equity at year end.

metrics.label: ROIC (FY26)
metrics.definition: After-tax EBIT ÷ invested capital at the start of the year. Invested capital excludes about ₹8k crore of cash and treasury, which is why it looks so high.

metrics.label: Revenue growth FY22–FY26
metrics.definition: Compound annual growth of revenue from FY22 to FY26.

metrics.label: Cash conversion (FY26)
metrics.definition: Operating cash flow ÷ profit for the year.

metrics.label: Beta vs NIFTY 50
metrics.definition: Sensitivity of DABUR's daily return to the NIFTY 50's, over the two years to the price date.

flags.title: Two cash-flow lines are swapped in the FY22 file
flags.text: The exchange file for FY22 files the purchase of property, plant and equipment under the proceeds-from-sale tag and the proceeds under the purchase tag, which made FY22 capital expenditure look tiny. The printed cash-flow statement of the next year's results is used instead, and the check is shown as a warning, not as passed.

limitations: Template A (non-financial, positive free cash flow). Single-stage fade model; no currency driver.
Cash flows are discounted to the balance-sheet date, 30 Sep 2026, two months before the price date; the model does not roll that gap forward, so its values are slightly low against the price.
Debt is borrowings plus lease liabilities; earmarked bank balances are counted as cash, which overstates cash slightly.
The risk-free rate is a twelve-month average while the price and equity risk premium are point-in-time.
The event study measures the size of a move, not its cause; five results days are too few for statistical claims.

Dabur files its purchases and sales of investments under the exchange's 'investment property' cash-flow tags. They are cash-flow detail that does not enter the valuation, and they are shown under their own labels rather than as investment property.

From FY23 the figures come from the exchange XBRL filings; the FY22 balance sheet and the lease liabilities for FY23 to FY25 come from the results PDFs (text layers checked against the printed subtotals and the XBRL).
The quarterly view covers fewer quarters than the pages of companies whose older filings were also loaded.
Static page: prices are end-of-day as of the date shown, not live.
